questions.prompt: A Node bundle builds but a package disappears after production pruning. Which check catches the deployment gap?

options.label: Only checking that the bundle file exists.
Safe startup of the final pruned artifact in an isolated environment.
Another source-only module compile against populated local node_modules.

questions.explanation: The deployed dependency graph can differ from local source tests. Boot the actual artifact with inert I/O; compilation and file presence are insufficient.

questions.prompt: A release writes a new data shape then fails. What must rollback planning consider?

options.label: Compatibility and recovery for persisted data and external effects as well as code.
Assume reverting the code reverses every database and remote mutation.
Delete all new records without considering ownership or recovery.

questions.explanation: Application rollback does not undo data or remote effects. Compatibility and reconciliation require explicit planning; destructive cleanup is not a generic rollback.

questions.prompt: A customer-specific policy differs from another customer. How should reusable design proceed?

options.label: Hardcode tenant names throughout the shared runtime.
Build a universal framework before investigating the second workflow.
Identify shared invariants and keep explicit policy differences at a boundary.

questions.explanation: Evidence should guide abstraction. Scattered special cases obstruct maintenance; speculative generalization can encode the wrong common model.

questions.prompt: A pilot is about to become an ongoing customer dependency. What must be established?

options.label: An assumption that someone will monitor it later.
A named operational owner, support boundary and tested recovery instructions.
Only the original builder's private notes.

questions.explanation: Sustained service requires accessible ownership and recovery. Private knowledge and unspecified monitoring create an unsupported dependency.
